name: Nurse outfit
blurb: Classic white dress and cap or modern scrubs: nurse costume parts and history
title: Nurse Outfit: Classic Costume vs Modern Scrubs Reference
description: Nurse outfit reference: the classic white dress, apron and cap, modern scrubs, how nurse uniforms changed, drawing tips and costume advice for cosplayers.
answer: A nurse outfit in costume and character design usually means the classic nurse uniform: a white or pale dress, sometimes with an apron, and a small white cap. Real nurses today mostly wear scrubs, a loose short-sleeved top and trousers, so the cap-and-dress look is now mainly a costume or a period detail.

body: Uniforms for nurses became common in the 19th century as nursing turned into a trained profession. Many were based on the clothing of religious nursing orders or domestic workers: a long dress, a white apron and a cap. Over the 20th century hems rose, aprons disappeared and caps were dropped by most hospitals for hygiene and practicality.

Modern scrubs, plain tops and trousers in solid colours, are easy to wash and change. In fiction the classic white outfit signals a caring or gentle character, while scrubs give a more realistic, medical-drama feel.

sections.h: How to draw a nurse outfit

ul: The cap is a small folded shape on top of the head; it sits behind the fringe and needs hair or pins to hold it, so keep it tilted with the head.
Button-front dresses have a straight placket down the centre; line the buttons up even when the body turns.
Use pale colours with a darker accent at the belt or piping so the white does not wash out.
Scrubs are loose and boxy; draw short sleeves wide around the arms and trousers that fold over the shoes.
Props help: a clipboard, a stethoscope around the neck or a pocket with pens.

body: Choose a clear era and stay with it; mixing scrubs with a vintage cap looks confused. Keep the outfit clean and pressed, since a nurse uniform is about neatness. Avoid using the red cross emblem on costumes: it is a protected symbol under international law, so many designers use a pink heart or a plus sign in another colour instead.

Friendly, helpful poses suit the character: holding a clipboard to the chest, offering a hand, or checking a watch. Bright, even lighting matches the clinical setting, while warm light makes it feel gentle.

faq.a: Very rarely. Most hospitals stopped using nurse caps decades ago, and nurses now usually wear scrubs.

faq.q: Why shouldn't a nurse costume use a red cross?
faq.a: The red cross on white is a protected emblem for medical and humanitarian services under the Geneva Conventions, so costume and game designers usually replace it.
Scrubs are simple, washable tops and trousers worn by medical staff, usually in a single solid colour.
